event.title: Alberta votes on non-binding question about pursuing a later binding separation referendum
event.what_happened: Albertans are voting on whether Alberta should remain a province of Canada or whether the provincial government should begin the legal process required to hold a binding referendum later on separation from Canada.
who: separatist organizers including Cory Morgan, Mitch Sylvestre and Jeffrey Rath
event.event_date_basis: Packet 1: "People in the province of Alberta head to the polls on Monday..." with packet publication on 2026-10-19; Packet 4 explicitly says, "please vote ... on October 19th."

latest_development.summary: Voting is underway in Alberta on the non-binding separation question; ballots will be counted by hand, with the separation question counted first and results expected in the early hours of Tuesday.

packets.note: Main same-day report on voting and expected count timing.

confirmed_facts.fact: Albertans are voting on 2026-10-19 on whether Alberta should remain in Canada or whether the provincial government should begin the legal process for a later binding referendum on separation.
The Oct. 19 vote itself is non-binding.
Question 10 is a choice question, and Elections Alberta says it will be counted first.
Ballots will be counted by hand.

Packet 1 says election officials have 48 hours to complete the count, starting no earlier than 20:00 local time on Monday, and that separation-question results should be available in the early hours of Tuesday.
The ballot also includes nine other referendum questions in addition to the separation question.
Danielle Smith says she opposes separation and will vote to keep Alberta in Canada.
Prime Minister Mark Carney publicly urged Albertans to vote against separation at a Forever Canadian rally in Edmonton before voting day.
A grassroots pro-separation petition gathered about 300,000 signatures earlier in 2026.
An anti-separation petition was signed by more than 400,000 people.
Elections Alberta says Alberta has been in a referendum period since 2026-03-31, and for Question 10 since 2026-05-28.
A court ruling blocked a binding referendum on separation unless First Nations were first consulted about effects on treaty rights, according to the reporting and explainer packets.

chronology.event: Alberta entered a referendum period under Elections Alberta rules.
The referendum period for Question 10, the separation question, began.
Danielle Smith announced she had voted against seceding, according to Al Jazeera.
Mark Carney delivered remarks at the Forever Canadian rally in Edmonton urging Albertans to vote for Canada.
Albertans began voting on the non-binding separation question and nine other referendum questions.
Packet 1 says results on the separation question should be available in the early hours of Tuesday after hand counting begins Monday evening.

background.fact: Earlier in 2026, Smith called the vote after a grassroots group gathered about 300,000 signatures on a petition seeking a binding referendum on separation.
Last year, Smith's government made it easier to start referendums, according to Al Jazeera.
A second petition opposing separation collected more than 400,000 signatures.

legal.statement: On 2026-10-19, Albertans are voting on a non-binding choice question about whether Alberta should remain in Canada or whether the government should commence the legal process for a later binding referendum on separation.
If the legal-process option wins, the government says it would start the legal processes necessary to hold a binding referendum on separation at a later date.
A court decision found that a binding referendum on separation could not be held without consultation with First Nations on potential effects on treaty rights.

reconciled.discrepancy: Some news packets place Carney's Edmonton Forever Canadian rally on Thursday, while Fox places it on Friday.
reconciled.resolution: Use 2026-10-16 for the rally date based on the official Prime Minister transcript/record in Packet 6.

unverified: Packet 4 says the Alberta government is appealing the court decision; no separate packet independently confirms the appeal filing.
Packet 2 says that as of Saturday more than 1.2 million Albertans had cast a ballot, but the excerpt does not identify an official source for that figure.
Packet 2's Globe and Mail-based assertions about separatist leaders' contacts with U.S. Republican strategists and State Department officials are not independently corroborated in the packet set.
missing_evidence: Official Elections Alberta turnout figures and official vote results once counting begins.
Primary poll releases or methodology documents for the Abacus Data and Angus Reid polling cited in Packet 2, including fieldwork dates and exact question wording.
The actual court decision and any appeal filing to verify the scope and procedural status of the First Nations consultation ruling.
A clearly dated official publication record for Packet 4's explainer page.
angle: Albertans are voting today on a non-binding separation question that would not itself split the province from Canada but could start the legal process toward a later binding referendum; the immediate coverage hook is that voting is underway and the separation question will be counted first, with results expected early Tuesday.
